hints: Focus on the Hess cycle idea for formation data, products are made and reactants are unmade.
Add up the formation enthalpies for the products, $(-635 + 228)$, and separately for the reactants, $(-60 + -286)$.
Finish with products minus reactants and watch the double negative carefully to get the small exothermic value.
walkthrough:
**Recall the rule for formation data**

Think of it simply. To go from reactants to products, you first break reactants back to elements, then make products from elements.

That gives the golden rule:
$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{reactants})$$

**Add up products and reactants separately**

Do not rush into one long line. Keep the two totals tidy.

For products:
$$(-635 + 228) = -407 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

For reactants:
$$(-60 + -286) = -346 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Subtract to find the reaction enthalpy**

Now apply products minus reactants.
$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = -407 - (-346)$$

Be careful, minus a negative becomes plus:
$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = -407 + 346 = -61 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

The negative sign tells you the reaction is slightly exothermic.

options.A: Incorrect. This adds all four values together: $(-635 + 228 - 60 - 286) = -753$. You must subtract the reactant total, not add it.
options.B: Correct. Products minus reactants gives $(-635 + 228) - (-60 - 286) = -407 + 346 = -61 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Well done for handling the signs carefully.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the same magnitude but the wrong sign. It comes from doing reactants minus products instead of products minus reactants.
options.D: Incorrect. This is the reverse of option A, adding everything and then reversing the sign. Remember the rule is always products minus reactants for formation data.
